titre: Perkin was looking for quinine, the structure of his mauve dates from 1994
accroche: In 1856, an 18-year-old student aims for an antimalarial and obtains the first commercially sold synthetic dye. Its structure was not corrected until 1994.
contenu_vulgarise:
During the Easter vacation of 1856, an eighteen-year-old student works at home on a problem his professor mentioned. He misses the drug he was after and obtains the first commercially sold synthetic dye. The happy accident is what people usually remember. A decisive chapter of the story dates from 1994.

## An atomic tally

William Perkin studies at the Royal College of Chemistry in London, under August Hofmann. Hofmann has pointed out how useful it would be to synthesize quinine, the antimalarial then obtained only from cinchona bark. Perkin tries his hand at it in the evenings and on weekends.

On paper, the tally is tempting. Quinine has the formula C₂₀H₂₄N₂O₂. Two molecules of allyltoluidine, of formula C₁₀H₁₃N, plus oxygen, minus one molecule of water, give exactly those atoms. The accounts differ on the starting material: Imperial College has Perkin starting from allyltoluidine, the Science Museum from aniline. In the latter's account, oxidizing aniline with potassium dichromate leaves a black precipitate, and the solution drawn from it dyes silk purple.

## Against his master's advice

Perkin files a patent on August 26, 1856 for a coloring matter giving lilac or purple on silk, cotton, or wool. Hofmann advises him against commercializing it. Perkin does so anyway, with money from his father, a building contractor, who finances the Greenford Green factory near Harrow. In December 1857, the firm of Perkin and Sons begins supplying mauve to silk dyers.

## The structure that waits until 1994

The dye is called mauveine. Its structure, accepted for decades, is corrected in 1994 by O. Meth-Cohn and M. Smith, in a paper titled “What did W. H. Perkin actually make when he oxidised aniline to obtain mauveine?” Three changes: the group at position 7 is an aminotolyl and not an aminophenyl, the phenyl sits at position 5 and not the tolyl, and a methyl occupies position 9 instead of 8.

The dye, moreover, is not a single molecule. It comprises two main components that differ by one methyl group, and others have been identified since: twelve mauveines and pseudomauveines in 2008, according to Wikipedia.

These methyls have an origin. They come from toluidines, which pure aniline does not contain. Mauveine A combines two units of aniline, one of p-toluidine, and one of o-toluidine. The Imperial College page describes the synthesis as the oxidation of a mixture of methylanilines: the original dye presupposes an impure starting point.

## The displacement

This story is not just a happy accident. The first commercially sold synthetic dye fed an industry, then that of pharmaceuticals, for 138 years without its exact structure being established. Chemistry can make and sell a substance before knowing exactly what it is, and a formula printed in textbooks is not a proven formula.

repere.texte: Perkin obtains mauve in 1856, at 18, during the Easter vacation; in 1857 he opens the Greenford Green factory, near London, with his father's financial backing.

carte.punch: Perkin's mauve was born in 1856. Its structure was not corrected until 1994.
carte.idee: In 1856, William Perkin, 18, tries to make quinine and obtains a purple dye, the first commercially sold synthetic dye. In 1994, Meth-Cohn and Smith show that the accepted structure of mauveine was incorrect. The dye is, moreover, a mixture.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Meth-Cohn and Smith — What did W. H. Perkin actually make when he oxidised aniline to obtain mauveine?
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The 1994 paper that corrects the structure of mauveine. The DOI is resolved by Crossref (title, authors, journal, and year confirmed) and redirects to the publisher's page, which refuses automated access; the revision is reported by the Imperial College page.

quiz.question: What did the 1994 analysis establish about Perkin's mauveine?
choix: The structure accepted until then for mauveine was incorrect
Perkin had in fact made quinine, without knowing it
The dye actually contains no nitrogen atom
The purple obtained came from a mineral pigment, not an organic compound
quiz.explication: Meth-Cohn and Smith corrected the accepted structure of mauveine in 1994, 138 years after the 1856 patent. The dye itself comprises two main components that differ by one methyl.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who financed the Greenford Green factory where Perkin produces his dye?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Perkin sets up the factory with his father's money, a building contractor's, despite Hofmann's reservations about selling the dye.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What was Perkin aiming for when working at home in the evenings and on weekends, under Hofmann's direction?
choix: Developing a durable varnish for silk
Synthesizing quinine, an antimalarial drawn from cinchona
Finding a substitute for natural indigo
Reproducing the purple color of Tyrian purple
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Hofmann had pointed out the value of synthesizing quinine, the antimalarial then obtained only from cinchona bark.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the reconstructed composition of mauveine A show?
choix: That it derives from natural indigo
That it is only a single pure molecule
That it comes from unconverted quinine
That it combines aniline, p-toluidine, and o-toluidine
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Mauveine A combines aniline, p-toluidine, and o-toluidine, which shows an impure starting point.
